key_insight: Process-zone condensation reduces nonlinear composite-cell solves without training while remaining exact relative to the full discretization as long as the eliminated region stays elastic.
engineering_relevance: The method can accelerate FE² simulations of composites with fibre–matrix debonding and matrix plasticity while preserving macroscopic stress and consistent tangent accuracy.
method: Schur-condense the linear elastic remainder, retaining all interface and process-zone internal variables.
Recover macroscopic stress and consistent tangent using influence matrices.
Back-substitute once per increment to check elasticity outside the retained zone and expand it when needed.
evidence_signal: Eight of nine 2D paths matched full-cell stress and tangent to 1e-11, with the ninth flagged; aggregate 2D path speed-up was 3.3× excluding setup and checks, while adaptive plate FE² achieved 1.51× for glass/polypropylene.
watch_item: Speed-up is not guaranteed: certified 3D zones showed none, glass/epoxy plate simulations were slower, and efficiency depends on zone size, active sets and adaptation costs.
paper_title: Process-zone condensation: a discretization-exact reduced cell model for FE$^2$ analysis of composites with fibre-matrix debonding and matrix plasticity
